sections.heading: Professional summary
sections.content: Aditya More is a Data Scientist and Machine Learning Engineer with an M.S. in Computer Science from Clemson University. He builds end-to-end data science and machine learning systems, from data preprocessing and model development through evaluation and deployment. His interests include machine learning, deep learning, large language models, computer vision, AI security, MLOps, and retrieval-augmented generation.

sections.heading: Researcher - LLM Agents and Human Behavior at Clemson University
sections.content: Aditya has served as a Researcher in Clemson University's School of Computing from May 2026 to the present, based in Clemson, South Carolina and working remotely. Under the supervision of Dr. Long Cheng, he investigates whether Large Language Model agents can realistically simulate human behavior and how behavioral fidelity can be systematically evaluated. His research covers LLM agents, multi-agent systems, Generative AI, human behavior simulation, and AI evaluation. He is conducting a literature review of LLM-based human behavior simulation, autonomous agents, multi-agent systems, and AI-generated synthetic populations; investigating AgentSociety, YuLan-OneSim, Generative Agents, and MiroFish; and developing a taxonomy spanning decision-making, social interaction, cooperation, trust, and other behavioral dimensions. He is designing and reproducing behavioral experiments including Trust Games and Dictator Games to compare LLM-agent decisions with established human behavioral data, and exploring benchmarks for behavioral realism, consistency, and human-agent similarity. The work is building toward a survey of the strengths and limitations of LLM agents for simulating human behavior and whether AI agents can support or partially substitute human participants in early-stage studies. Technologies and research tools include Python, Large Language Models, Multi-Agent Systems, AgentSociety, YuLan-OneSim, Generative Agents, MiroFish, literature review, experimental design, and behavioral evaluation.

sections.heading: Graduate Student Hourly — Clemson University
sections.content: Aditya worked as a Graduate Student Hourly in Data Science at Clemson University's School of Computing in Clemson, South Carolina, from August 2024 through December 2025. He designed Jupyter Notebook labs and assignments for a graduate Applied Data Science course; built automated nbgrader pipelines and submission-validation logic; and created exercises covering preprocessing, IQR and Z-score outlier detection, model selection, cross-validation, feature selection, and PCA. He supported students through weekly office hours, collaborated with faculty on curriculum and Coursera deployment, and diagnosed autograder issues reported through Salesforce tickets before validating and deploying corrected notebooks. Technologies included Python, Jupyter, scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy, nbgrader, and Coursera.

sections.heading: Software Engineer — Amdocs
sections.content: Aditya worked as a Software Engineer at Amdocs in Pune, India, from October 2021 through December 2022. He performed end-to-end, regression, and API testing for enterprise telecom systems serving AT&T; designed test cases and validation strategies for production releases; and automated test workflows with Postman and proprietary tools. He collaborated with cross-functional teams in the United States and India in an Agile environment and participated in feature planning, requirements analysis, and validation across multiple releases. Technologies included Postman and Selenium.

sections.heading: BB-8 AI-Powered Portfolio Assistant
sections.content: BB-8 is the active AI co-pilot for Aditya's Tech Portfolio. It uses the OpenAI Responses and Embeddings APIs with a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline over structured, verified portfolio data. Semantic retrieval is backed by Amazon S3 Vectors when configured, with a deterministic local keyword retriever as a development and availability fallback. The system retrieves relevant chunks, supplies only those chunks to the language model, returns source-page links with answers, preserves chat state while navigating, and includes a retrieval evaluation dataset. The application is built with Next.js, TypeScript, React, and the AWS SDK. BB-8 Local is a separate experimental personal language-model project and is not the model serving the live assistant.

sections.heading: Personalized Movie Recommendation System
sections.content: Completed in 2024, this end-to-end recommendation system combined MovieLens, TMDB, and IMDb data: more than 26 million ratings, 270,000 users, and 45,000 movies. Aditya implemented collaborative filtering, content-based models, matrix factorization with FunkSVD, and neural methods. FunkSVD achieved RMSE 0.76, approximately a 21 percent improvement over baseline. He designed ETL pipelines and optimized sparse-matrix computations. Technologies included Python, scikit-learn, PyTorch, Flask, PostgreSQL, Docker, and recommender-system methods.

sections.heading: Skynet — AQI Prediction System
sections.content: Completed in 2025, Skynet is an end-to-end machine-learning pipeline for forecasting Air Quality Index. It integrated NASA TEMPO, OpenAQ, weather, and traffic APIs; implemented ingestion and preprocessing pipelines; engineered environmental and traffic features; and modeled temporal and spatial AQI patterns. Technologies included Python, scikit-learn, pandas, and NumPy.

sections.heading: R2D2 — Experimental Transformer-based LLM
sections.content: R2D2 is an in-progress 2025 research project that builds transformer architectures from scratch to study language-model internals and training dynamics. It implements tokenization, embeddings, and attention mechanisms; trains small-scale transformer models; and explores LLM behavior and optimization. Technologies include Python, PyTorch, Transformers, NLP, and deep learning. R2D2 is distinct from the active BB-8 portfolio co-pilot.

sections.heading: Adversarial Attacks — Experimentation and Case Study
sections.content: This 2024 Clemson AI-security case study examined data poisoning, adversarial patches, and evasion attacks on computer-vision models. Aditya experimented with monocular depth-estimation systems used in autonomous-vehicle perception, analyzed effects on scene understanding and depth pipelines, and evaluated attack transferability across models and threat settings. Technologies and areas included Python, computer vision, deep learning, adversarial machine learning, and AI security.

sections.heading: LLM Defense Evaluation Framework
sections.content: From September through December 2024, Aditya built automated pipelines for jailbreak testing and defense evaluation of large language models. The framework evaluated token-level patterns, semantic behavior, refusal mechanisms, response consistency, latency, and attack success rates, and benchmarked multiple models under diverse jailbreak strategies. Technologies and areas included Python, LLM evaluation, adversarial AI, and AI security.

sections.heading: NeuralLog — Intelligent Activity Tracking System
sections.content: Completed in 2025, NeuralLog is a personal machine-learning system that tracks tasks, routines, and habits; analyzes behavioral patterns; and generates personalized productivity insights. Technologies included Python, machine learning, and data analysis.

Technologies included TensorFlow and OpenCV. The source repository is https://github.com/Skywalker1910/Covid-19-Safeguard.
